EXERCISE
AP®︎/COLLEGE BIOLOGY
Photosynthesis
Test your knowledge of photosynthesis!

VIDEO
AP®︎/COLLEGE BIOLOGY
Photosynthesis
Photosynthesis is essential for life on Earth. Photosynthesis involves two stages: the light-dependent reactions, which require sunlight and water to produce oxygen, ATP, and NADPH, and the light-independent reactions (or "dark reactions"), which use the products of the light-dependent reactions along with carbon dioxide to produce carbohydrates.

EXERCISE
HIGH SCHOOL BIOLOGY
Apply: Photosynthesis
Apply your understanding of photosynthesis in this set of free, standards-aligned practice questions.

EXERCISE
HIGH SCHOOL BIOLOGY
Understand: Photosynthesis
Check your understanding of photosynthesis in this set of free, standards-aligned practice questions.

VIDEO
HIGH SCHOOL BIOLOGY
Photosynthesis
The process of photosynthesis converts light energy to stored chemical energy by converting carbon dioxide plus water into sugars plus released oxygen. Photosynthesis occurs in two phases: the light-dependent reactions, and the light-independent reactions.

LESSON
HIGH SCHOOL BIOLOGY
Photosynthesis
Understand how photoautotrophs convert light energy, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose and oxygen. Break down the stages of photosynthesis to see how this process supports nearly all ecosystems by producing the carbohydrates that fuel heterotrophs.

LESSON
AP®︎/COLLEGE BIOLOGY
Photosynthesis
Explore how light-dependent reactions capture energy to produce ATP and NADPH. Understand how the Calvin cycle uses these molecules to fix carbon and build sugars. Discover the evolutionary origins of photosynthesis and examine how this process sustains ecosystems by driving energy flow and oxygen production.
